nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type whose Boolean equality agrees with equality, and write $|t|$ for the length of a list $t$. For every pattern $p$ and text $t$ over $\alpha$ and every natural number $s$, the naive matcher run on $p$ and $t$ reports the shift $s$ if and only if $p$ matches $t$ at $s$, that is, $s \le |t|$ and $p$ is a prefix of the suffix of $t$ obtained by dropping its first $s$ symbols.
nodes.title: Correctness of naive string matching

nodes.summary: For every text $t$ of length $n$, the naive matcher run on the empty pattern and $t$ reports exactly the shifts $0, 1, \dots, n$ in increasing order and performs no symbol comparisons.
nodes.title: Naive matching with the empty pattern

nodes.summary: If the pattern $p$ is longer than the text $t$, then the naive matcher run on $p$ and $t$ reports no shifts and performs no symbol comparisons.
nodes.title: Naive matching with a pattern longer than the text

nodes.summary: For every pattern $p$ and text $t$, the list of shifts reported by the naive matcher on $p$ and $t$ is strictly increasing; in particular, no shift is reported twice.
nodes.title: Naive matching reports shifts in increasing order

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type whose Boolean equality is reflexive, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $m \le n$ be natural numbers. On the pattern consisting of $m$ copies of $x$ and the text consisting of $n$ copies of $x$, the naive matcher reports exactly the shifts $0, 1, \dots, n - m$ in increasing order, so all overlapping occurrences are reported.
nodes.title: Naive matching on a repeated symbol reports every shift

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a pattern of length $m$ and $t$ a text of length $n$. If $m \le n$, the list of shifts reported by the naive matcher on $p$ and $t$ is the increasing list of all $s \in \{0, \dots, n - m\}$ such that $p$ is a prefix of the suffix of $t$ starting at the zero-based position $s$, with symbols compared by the Boolean equality of the alphabet. If $m > n$, the list is empty.
nodes.title: Output of naive matching

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ be a pattern and $t = t_0 \cdots t_{n-1}$ a text. If $m \le n$, the number of symbol comparisons performed by the naive matcher on $p$ and $t$ is
nodes.title: Exact comparison count of naive matching

nodes.summary: For a pattern of length $m$ and a text of length $n$, the naive matcher performs at most $(n - m + 1) \cdot m$ symbol comparisons if $m \le n$, and no comparisons if $m > n$.
nodes.title: Upper bound on the comparisons of naive matching

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type whose Boolean equality is reflexive, let $x \in \alpha$, and let $m \le n$ be natural numbers. On the pattern consisting of $m$ copies of $x$ and the text consisting of $n$ copies of $x$, the naive matcher performs exactly $(n - m + 1) \cdot m$ symbol comparisons.
nodes.title: Comparison count of naive matching on a repeated symbol

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 \cdots p_{m-1}$ be a pattern and $t = t_0 \cdots t_{n-1}$ a text over an alphabet with a Boolean equality test. If $m \le n$, the naive matcher handles the shifts $s = 0, 1, \dots, n - m$ in turn: it compares $p_i$ with $t_{s+i}$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots$ until a comparison fails or all $m$ symbols are compared, and it reports $s$ if no comparison failed. It returns the reported shifts in the order found,…
nodes.title: Naive string matcher

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
